sol.def: A day on Mars: about 24 hours and 40 minutes.

regolith.def: The layer of dust and rock fragments that covers the Moon and other airless worlds.

lander.def: A spacecraft that sets down on a surface and works without moving from its spot.

rover.def: A wheeled vehicle that drives across the surface of another world.

orbiter.def: A spacecraft that circles a world without landing on it.

probe.def: A spacecraft that travels far away to explore; the Pioneers are probes.

descent-stage.def: The base of the Apollo lunar module: it landed on the Moon and stayed there.

ascent-stage.def: The top part of the lunar module, which lifted off with the astronauts to return to the spacecraft in orbit.

seismometer.def: An instrument that measures vibrations of the ground.

magnitude.def: A number that tells how much energy a quake released.

retroreflector.def: A set of prisms that sends light straight back where it came from; it is used to measure the distance to the Moon with lasers.

light-time.def: How long light, or a radio signal, takes to travel from one place to another.

au.def: The average distance between Earth and the Sun: 149,597,870.7 km.

orbital-elements.def: Six numbers that describe the shape, size and orientation of an orbit.

eccentricity.def: How far an orbit is from being a perfect circle.

kepler-equation.def: A formula that links time with the position of a body along its orbit.

barycenter.def: The balance point that two bodies, like Earth and the Moon, orbit around.

sublimation.def: Going straight from solid to gas, without becoming liquid.

perchlorate.def: A salt that contains chlorine and oxygen; Phoenix found it in the soil of Mars.

silica.def: A mineral made of silicon and oxygen; when abundant, it is a clue to hot water in the past.

brine.def: Water with a lot of dissolved salt.

sodium-carbonate.def: A white salt that forms the bright spots of Occator crater, on Ceres.

dust-devil.def: A whirlwind that lifts dust; on Mars it sometimes cleaned solar panels.

dust-storm.def: A storm that can cover almost all of Mars and darken the Sun for weeks.

solar-panel.def: A surface that turns sunlight into electricity.

rtg.def: A source of electricity that uses the heat of a radioactive material; it does not depend on the Sun.

ion-propulsion.def: An engine that shoots out charged atoms at high speed: a very gentle push, but for a very long time.

xenon.def: A noble gas that Dawn used as fuel for its ion engine.

hydrazine.def: Fuel for the small thrusters that point a spacecraft.

transit.def: When a planet passes in front of its star and dims it slightly.

light-curve.def: A graph of a star's brightness over time.

exoplanet.def: A planet that orbits a star other than the Sun.

asteroid-belt.def: The zone between Mars and Jupiter with millions of rocky bodies.

gravity-assist.def: A maneuver that uses a planet's gravity to change a spacecraft's speed or direction.

heliosphere.def: The bubble the Sun's wind blows around it.

deep-space-network.def: NASA's network of large antennas around the world for talking to distant spacecraft.

carrier-signal.def: The basic radio wave that carries data; sometimes it is all that arrives from a distant spacecraft.

plaque.def: An engraved plate with a message, like those on the Pioneers or on Apollo 11.
